title: Zion’s inhabitants are called to exult in Israel’s Holy One
speaker: the redeemed people’s song in Isaiah’s oracle
note: Call to praise addressed to people; closes the song whose 12:4–5 calls are only a Study Context record (ot-isaiah-v12-4).

title: Babylon’s people are told to wail, for the Lord’s day is near
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah (oracle against Babylon)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Prophetic summons to wail, like recorded ot-isaiah-v23-6 and ot-jeremiah-v6-26.

title: A signal and the Lord’s command muster forces against Babylon
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
recipient: the consecrated forces mustered against Babylon
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list: 13:3–4 report the Lord’s command to the mustered army ('I command'; 'the Lord Sabaoth has commanded').

title: Israel is to take up a taunt against Babylon’s fallen king
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Scripted taunt ('you will take up this lament… and say'); compare future songs treated as Study Context (ot-isaiah-v12-4).

title: Moab is called to wail and mourn in sackcloth over its ruin
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah (oracle against Moab)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 15:3 (context verse, outside candidate list) continues the summons: sackcloth, beating, wailing. Isaiah 15 has no records.

title: Moab’s devourers are told to trample its vineyards as far as Iazer
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
recipient: the devourers of nations (invaders of Moab)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Summons to attackers, comparable to recorded ot-jeremiah-v5-10; 'Wander in the wilderness!' follows.

title: The watchman tells the inquirer from Seir to seek and stay near
speaker: the watchman in Isaiah’s vision
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reply to the call recorded at ot-isaiah-v21-11; a different speaker, so not an extension.

title: The Lord called Jerusalem to weeping, shaving and sackcloth
speaker: the Lord Sabaoth (reported by Isaiah)
note: Outside candidate list. Reported summons to mourn; ot-isaiah-v22-13 records the people feasting instead.

title: The Lord calls Eliakim and gives him the steward’s robe and authority
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Outside candidate list: 22:20 (I will call Eliakim) and 22:22–23 (David’s glory, established ruler) complete the appointment.

title: The ships of Carthage are told to wail over Tyre’s fall
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah (oracle concerning Tyre)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 23:14 (P01934) repeats the summons. The ships stand for their crews; compare recorded ot-isaiah-v23-6.

title: The earth’s people are told to wail over the vanished wine
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Imperative summons to wail amid the world judgment; Isaiah 24 has no records.

title: Hope belongs to the devout; woe to those who reject the law
speaker: voices from the ends of the earth (Isaiah’s oracle)
note: Woe-saying with its contrast of the devout and those who reject the law.

title: The hearer is told to deliver all these things to the nations
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Greek-based text has an imperative ('hand all these things over to the nations'); the addressee is unclear.

title: Women returning from a spectacle are summoned to come
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Brief summons inside the judgment oracle; its purpose is left unstated.

title: Unnamed gatherers are told to gather Israel’s sons one by one
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Command within the 'on that day' promise; compare recorded ot-isaiah-v43-6 (release My sons and daughters).

title: Woe to the proud crown of Ephraim’s drunken hirelings
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Woe against pride and drunkenness (28:7–8 continue), though mainly a judgment on Ephraim.

title: Honoring God with lips while the heart is far is vain worship
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
topic: Clean and Unclean, and the Tradition of the Elders
note: Outside candidate list. Jesus quotes 29:13 in Matthew 15:8–9 and Mark 7:6–7; link as Additional Scripture.

title: Woe to those who plan in secret and apart from the Lord
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Ethical woe, like recorded AUD-28-5-20; 30:1 ('a plan not through Me', context-adjacent, unrecorded) makes the same charge.

title: The Lord tells Isaiah to announce Egypt’s futility and write it down
speaker: the Lord
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 30:7 ('Announce to them, This consolation of yours is futile') opens the same charge to Isaiah.

title: Turning back to God brings salvation; trust in futile things fails
speaker: the Lord, Israel’s Holy One, through Isaiah
note: Outside candidate list (context verse). Call to return that was refused, like recorded ot-jeremiah-v6-16.

title: Blessed are those who remain in the Lord
speaker: Isaiah
note: Beatitude ('Blessed are those remaining in Him') after the promise that God waits to show mercy.

title: Woe to those trusting horses and chariots rather than the Holy One
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: 30:1–2 (woe to those going down to Egypt without asking God; unrecorded) is the same charge; link as Additional Scripture.

title: Blessed is the one with offspring and household in Zion
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Greek-text beatitude closing the Assyria oracle; more a blessing than counsel.

title: The fool plots harm against the lowly; the devout plan wisely
speaker: Isaiah
note: Wisdom contrast following 32:5 (Study Context ot-isaiah-v32-5); 32:8 is a context verse.

title: Isaiah summons the complacent wealthy women to hear and mourn
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: 32:9 ('rise and hear my voice') opens the address recorded at 32:10–12.

title: Blessed are those who sow beside every water
speaker: Isaiah
topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
note: Beatitude closing the promise of the Spirit’s renewal (32:15–20).

title: Woe to the destroyer: those who betray will be handed over
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Retribution woe, though mainly a judgment on Assyria. Isaiah 33 has no records.

title: Wisdom, knowledge and reverence for the Lord are true treasures
speaker: Isaiah
note: Outside candidate list; maxim inside a promise ('these are treasures of righteousness').

title: Whoever walks righteously and refuses bribes will dwell secure
speaker: Isaiah
note: Outside candidate list. Entrance saying like Greek Psalm 14: upright speech, no bribes, shunning bloodshed and injustice.

title: The Assyrian envoy dares Hezekiah to wager with the Assyrian king
speaker: Rapsakes, the Assyrian envoy
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 2 Kings 18:23 (the same challenge) is also unrecorded; link it as Additional Scripture.

title: The Assyrian envoy claims the Lord sanctioned his invasion
speaker: Rapsakes, the Assyrian envoy
note: This text keeps only the question 'have we come up without the Lord?'; 2 Kings 18:25 adds the claimed command.

title: The Assyrian envoy offers security and deportation in exchange for surrender
speaker: Rapsakes, the Assyrian envoy
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list: 36:17 finishes the offer begun in 36:16 (its parallel 2 Kings 18:32 is ot-2-kings-v18-32).

title: Hezekiah orders his people to give the envoy no answer
speaker: King Hezekiah (reported)
recipient: his officials and the people on the wall
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Parallel account of 2 Kings 18:36.

title: The Lord’s sign: eat the aftergrowth, then sow, reap and plant
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
recipient: Hezekiah and the remnant of Judah
topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
note: Parallel 2 Kings 19:29 is also unrecorded; link it as Additional Scripture.

title: Isaiah tells the ill Hezekiah to set his household in order
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Parallel account of 2 Kings 20:1.

title: All flesh is grass, but God’s word remains for ever
speaker: the prophet, answering the voice
topic: Minor Teachings: The Scriptures Read in Christ
note: Outside candidate list. 1 Peter 1:24–25 (A113) quotes this saying; 40:7–8 are unrecorded and 40:6 carries only the commission.

title: Those who wait for God renew their strength
speaker: Isaiah
note: Maxim-like promise to a class ('those enduring for God'), answering the complaint of 40:27.

title: The Lord puts His spirit on His servant to judge the nations
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
recipient: the Lord’s servant (named Jacob/Israel in this text)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 42:1 and 42:4 are outside the candidate list. Matthew 12:18–21 quotes it (inside AUD-44-12-15); the 42:5–9 commission is AUD-28-42-5.

title: The deaf and blind are summoned to listen and look
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
recipient: Israel, the spiritually deaf and blind
note: Call to perceive addressed to the people (42:19 names God’s servants); bare 'hear' summonses are often Study Context.

title: God tells Israel to remember and confess its lawless acts first
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: 'You, state your lawless acts first, so that you may be justified': a call to confession in the trial speech.

title: Know that the idolater’s heart is ashes and cannot save him
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Imperatives 'Know… See' close the idol satire; ot-isaiah-v44-21 then calls Israel to remember.

title: The Lord commissions His anointed Cyrus to free His people
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 44:28–45:1 and 45:3–6 are outside the candidate list. Cyrus’s call is also recalled in 41:2, 46:11 and 48:14–15.

title: Survivors of the nations are summoned to gather and consider together
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: 45:21 continues the summons ('let them draw near so that they may know together').

title: Heeding God’s commands would have brought peace like a river
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: 48:17 (context verse) presents the Lord as the one who shows the road; compare ot-jeremiah-v7-23.

title: The Lord names His servant and appoints him light to the nations
speaker: the Lord (reported by the servant)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list: 49:2–3 (equipped, and named 'My slave, Israel') begin the commission recorded at 49:5–6.

title: The servant is given as a covenant to free prisoners
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 49:8 ('I gave you as a covenant for nations… saying to those in bonds') begins the sentence recorded at 49:9.

title: The Lord gives His servant an instructed tongue and an open ear
speaker: the Lord (reported by the servant)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Third Servant Song: equipped for a speaking task, and obedient ('I do not disobey'); records at 50:8 and 50:10 follow.

title: Seekers of the Lord are told to look to Abraham and Sarah
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
recipient: those who pursue what is right and seek the Lord
note: 51:2 completes the same directive ('Look at Abraham your father and Sarah').

title: Do not fear mortal oppressors; remember God your Maker
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Same directive as 51:7 (do not fear human reproach): 'Recognize whom you dreaded… a mortal person'.

title: The thirsty are invited to come and eat without price
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
recipient: the thirsty and those without silver
note: 55:1 opens the invitation continued in 55:2; echoed in Revelation 22:17 (AUD-70-22-17) and John 7:37 (AUD-47-7-37).

title: The righteous are taken away from evil, yet no one considers it
speaker: Isaiah
note: 'See how the righteous man perished': a reflection rebuking indifference. Isaiah 57 has no records.

title: Those who hold fast to the Lord will inherit His holy mountain
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Contrasted with idols that cannot rescue (57:13a is sarcastic); a maxim-like promise to a class.

title: Clear the road and remove obstacles for God’s people
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah (quoted call)
recipient: those preparing the returning people’s road
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Same directive as 62:10 ('make a road… scatter the stones'); compare also 40:3.

title: The unjust are tossed like waves; the ungodly have no joy
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Outside candidate list. 48:22 (context verse) repeats 'There is no rejoicing for the ungodly'; link as Additional Scripture.

title: God rejects fasting joined to quarrels, oppression and outward show
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: 58:3 and 58:5 are context verses. Negative half of the fast teaching recorded at 58:6–7 (ot-isaiah-v58-6, ot-isaiah-v58-7).

title: The Lord appoints unceasing watchmen on Jerusalem’s walls
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Appointed guards 'will never be silent as they remember the Lord'; compare ot-isaiah-v21-6.

title: God looks to the humble who tremble at His word
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
note: Outside candidate list. Quoted in Acts 7:49–50 (A099, Study Context only); see also ot-isaiah-v66-5.

title: The Lord sends survivors to the nations and takes priests from them
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 66:20–21 are outside the candidate list. Foretold sending to announce God’s glory among the nations; priests and Levites taken from them.

title: God appoints Jeremiah a prophet before birth and sends him
speaker: the Lord
note: 1:5 is the appointment ('I have appointed you a prophet to nations'); 1:6 is the objection answered in 1:7.

title: The Lord puts His words in Jeremiah’s mouth, setting him over nations
speaker: the Lord
note: 1:9 is a context verse; the mandate is 'to uproot, demolish, destroy, build and plant'.

title: God tells Jeremiah to speak fearlessly, making him a fortified city
speaker: the Lord
note: 1:18–19 complete the charge: a fortified city and bronze wall against Judah’s kings, rulers and people.

title: Your own evil disciplines you; abandoning the Lord is bitter
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: 'Know and see that abandoning Me is bitter': maxim with a call to recognize it; 2:17 and 4:18 make the same point.

title: Israel is told to examine its ways and know what it did
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: Call to self-examination; the similar call in 3:2 is only a Study Context record (ot-jeremiah-v3-2).

title: A divorced wife who remarried may not return to her first husband
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
note: Cites the Deuteronomy 24:1–4 rule (C1166) as an image of Israel’s unfaithfulness; link as Additional Scripture.

title: God recalls calling faithless Israel to return to Him
speaker: the Lord (recalled to Jeremiah)
note: Reported earlier call ('I said, Return to Me. But she did not return'), like the recalled command ot-jeremiah-v7-23.

title: Israel is called to acknowledge its iniquity against the Lord
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: Content of the message Jeremiah is sent to proclaim (ot-jeremiah-v3-12); addressed to Israel, so a separate record.

title: Israel is called to return, renounce idols and swear truthfully
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: Outside candidate list. Conditional call to return, with the oath 'The Lord lives' sworn in truth, judgment and righteousness.

title: Judah is told to wear sackcloth and wail at the Lord’s fury
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Summons to mourn in the alarm oracle of 4:5–8 (ot-jeremiah-v4-5, ot-jeremiah-v4-6); compare ot-jeremiah-v6-26.

title: Heralds are told to warn the nations and Jerusalem of invaders
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 'Remind the nations… Announce in Jerusalem': a warning summons like ot-jeremiah-v4-5.

title: Jeremiah is given the answer to why the Lord brought disaster
speaker: the Lord
note: Scripted reply ('you will say to them'): they served foreign gods, so they will serve foreigners in a foreign land.

title: The message is to be announced to Jacob and proclaimed in Judah
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Introduces the address recorded as Study Context at 5:21 (ot-jeremiah-v5-21).

title: Offerings from those who reject God’s law are not acceptable
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: Follows 6:19 ('rejected My law'); compare AUD-09-15-22 (1 Samuel 15:22) and ot-hosea-v6-6.

title: The Lord appoints Jeremiah to test His people’s ways
speaker: the Lord
note: Appointment as assayer ('I have made you a tester'); 6:30 is Study Context (ot-jeremiah-v6-30).

title: Judah is told to amend its ways so God will settle it
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
recipient: all Judea at the Lord’s house
note: Core call of the temple sermon; 7:5–6 (ot-jeremiah-v7-5) spells out the amendment.

title: Judah is warned against trusting false words while breaking God’s commands
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: 7:8 repeats 7:4’s warning; 7:9 cites Decalogue prohibitions; 7:11 ('robbers’ cave') is quoted in Mark 11:17.

title: Judah is told to go to Shiloh and see what God did
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: Warning by example: what God did to Shiloh because of Israel’s evil.

summary: Isaiah 12–Jeremiah 7:12: most candidates are judgment or promise oracles; gaps are prophetic summonses, woes and beatitudes, servant, Cyrus and Jeremiah commissions, and Isaiah 36–38 parallels.
